what_it_does: Version-controlled container of folders and files with full per-file history
research_use: Single navigable workspace for data, code, docs and manuscript
traceability: Every file has a complete change history
limitations: Soft size limits; poor fit for large binary data (>100 MB/file)

what_it_does: Immutable ordered sequence of changes, each with author, timestamp, message and diff
research_use: Change record for every research artifact
traceability: Every change attributable to a person and time
limitations: History can be rewritten (force-push) unless the branch is protected

what_it_does: Line-level view of what changed in a commit and who last touched each line
research_use: See exactly what changed in a protocol, script or manuscript and by whom
traceability: Line-level authorship and change attribution
limitations: Binary and tabular data files do not diff meaningfully

what_it_does: GPG, SSH or S/MIME signature verification with a Verified badge
research_use: Assurance that a change came from the claimed author
traceability: Cryptographic identity integrity on the history
limitations: Setup friction; optional unless enforced by a ruleset

what_it_does: Attributes a single commit to multiple authors
research_use: Shared contribution credit for pair work
traceability: Multi-author attribution on individual changes
limitations: Convention only; not enforced

what_it_does: Stores large files as pointers in the repo with blobs on a separate store
research_use: Version mid-size datasets and figure bundles
traceability: Large artifacts get the same commit history as text
limitations: Storage and bandwidth quotas; not a data repository

what_it_does: Named immutable pointer to a specific commit
research_use: Mark project states (e.g. literature-complete)
traceability: Fixed, human-named reference points in history
limitations: Lightweight vs annotated tags behave differently

what_it_does: Marks a repo as a template; 'Use this template' seeds a fresh repo
research_use: Reusable research-project skeleton (this study's own template output)
traceability: New projects start from a known, documented structure
limitations: Copies only at creation; no later sync with the template

what_it_does: Org-level default CONTRIBUTING, issue/PR templates, CODE_OF_CONDUCT
research_use: Standardise practice across a group's repositories
traceability: Shared conventions are themselves versioned
limitations: Org defaults are overridden by repo-level files

what_it_does: Auto-rendered entry-point document for the repo and every folder
research_use: Project overview and folder-level data dictionaries
traceability: Documentation lives beside the artifacts it describes, with history
limitations: Single file per folder; long READMEs get unwieldy

what_it_does: Headings, tables, task lists, footnotes, alerts, code highlighting in .md and comments
research_use: Protocols, methodology and decision logs as versioned prose
traceability: Every documentation edit is a diffable commit
limitations: Plain text; no rich layout or reference management

what_it_does: Mermaid diagrams and LaTeX math rendered inside Markdown, issues and PRs
research_use: Workflow DAGs, lifecycle diagrams and equations without external tools
traceability: Diagrams version with the text
limitations: Mermaid feature lag; large diagrams hard to maintain

what_it_does: `- [ ]` checkboxes that render as tracked progress in issues and Markdown
research_use: Lightweight protocol steps and checklists
traceability: Checkbox state changes appear in the issue timeline
limitations: Not a real task system unless inside issues/Projects

what_it_does: Separate Git-backed documentation space per repository
research_use: Extended methodology handbook or lab manual
traceability: Versioned, but in a history separate from the code
limitations: Weaker cross-linking to issues/code; often better kept in-repo

what_it_does: Publishes a static site from a repo branch or folder
research_use: Public project site, rendered documentation, HTML reports
traceability: Published site is built from a specific commit
limitations: Static only; build constraints; extra config

what_it_does: Structured citation-metadata file rendered as 'Cite this repository'
research_use: Machine-readable attribution; consumed by Zenodo on release
traceability: Citation info is versioned with the project
limitations: Manual upkeep; authorship must be maintained by hand

what_it_does: Commit-pinned URLs to a file or line range
research_use: Cite an exact protocol step or result location from issues or the manuscript
traceability: Reference stays valid because it is pinned to a commit
limitations: Breaks conceptually if the referenced file is later restructured

what_it_does: Titled, threaded, stateful unit of work or discussion
research_use: Research tasks, methodological questions, decision threads, research-question tracking
traceability: Full chronological timeline of every change to the issue
limitations: Flat by default; needs conventions to distinguish task types

what_it_does: YAML or Markdown templates that structure new issues into fields
research_use: Enforce fields for decision records, data requests, analysis tasks
traceability: Structured, comparable records across issues of the same kind
limitations: Templates guide but are not strictly enforced

what_it_does: Org-defined type (Task, Bug, custom) on each issue
research_use: Classify issues as question / decision / analysis at the type level
traceability: Type is a first-class, filterable attribute
limitations: Organisation-scoped; limited number of types

what_it_does: Parent/child issue hierarchy with progress roll-up
research_use: Decompose a research phase into tasks; hierarchical planning
traceability: Parent shows completion state of its children
limitations: Depth and count limits

what_it_does: Up to 10 users marked responsible for an issue
research_use: Record who owns each research task
traceability: Responsibility is explicit and in the timeline
limitations: People only; teams cannot be assignees

what_it_does: Mentioning #123, a commit SHA or a PR creates a bidirectional link recorded in both timelines
research_use: Connect research question -> task -> commit -> PR -> release
traceability: The primary mechanism for linking research activities and artifacts
limitations: Manual; relies on contributors actually referencing

what_it_does: 'Closes #12' in a commit or PR auto-closes and links the issue on merge
research_use: Bind the resolution of a task to the change that resolved it
traceability: Automatic task-to-evidence link
limitations: Only closes; wrong keyword silently does nothing

what_it_does: Chronological record of every label, assignee, reference, comment, close and reopen
research_use: Reconstruct how a task or decision evolved and why
traceability: High-fidelity audit trail per issue
limitations: Not exportable as a structured record without the API

what_it_does: Emoji reactions; @user and @team notifications
research_use: Lightweight agreement signal; pull the right people into a thread
traceability: Agreement is visible but not a formal record
limitations: Reactions are weak evidence of a decision

what_it_does: Up to three issues pinned to the top of the issue list
research_use: Surface the roadmap or 'start here' issue
traceability: Entry points are stable and visible
limitations: Only three; repo-scoped

what_it_does: Table, board and roadmap over issues, PRs and draft items
research_use: Research roadmap, phase tracking, lifecycle board
traceability: Work items carry planning metadata across their whole life
limitations: Lives outside the repo; item caps; learning curve

what_it_does: Text, number, date, single-select and iteration fields on project items
research_use: 'Research phase', 'Related RQ', 'Artifact', 'Priority' fields per item
traceability: Planning attributes are queryable and groupable
limitations: Field values live on the project, not on the issue itself

what_it_does: Saved, filtered, grouped views of the same items
research_use: Board by status, roadmap by phase over time, table by artifact
traceability: One dataset, many audiences
limitations: View config is per-project; no cross-project views

what_it_does: Time-based Gantt-like view driven by date or iteration fields
research_use: Visualise the research timeline and phase durations
traceability: Schedule is derived from item fields
limitations: No dependency arrows; basic vs a real Gantt tool

what_it_does: Auto-set item status on events (added, PR merged, issue closed)
research_use: Keep the board current without manual moves
traceability: Status transitions are automatic and consistent
limitations: Small fixed set of triggers and actions

what_it_does: Burn-up and custom charts over project fields
research_use: Progress transparency; phase-completion trend
traceability: Progress is visualised from live data
limitations: History depth varies; limited chart types

what_it_does: Project-only notes not yet promoted to real issues
research_use: Capture ideas and candidate questions before formalising them
traceability: Not traceable until converted to an issue
limitations: No timeline, labels or cross-refs while a draft

what_it_does: Named bucket with an optional due date grouping issues and PRs
research_use: Research phases (literature complete, analysis complete)
traceability: Groups a body of work under a named phase
limitations: One milestone per issue; repo-scoped, not cross-repo

what_it_does: Automatic percent-complete from closed vs open items
research_use: Phase-completion signal for the whole team
traceability: Progress derived from the underlying issues
limitations: Coarse; only counts issues, not effort

what_it_does: Coloured, named tag on issues and PRs, scoped to the repo
research_use: Classify by activity: literature, methodology, data, analysis, decision, manuscript
traceability: Every labelled/unlabelled change is in the timeline
limitations: Flat (no hierarchy); per-repo; needs manual governance

what_it_does: Seed a consistent label set across repositories
research_use: Group-wide classification scheme
traceability: Shared taxonomy across projects
limitations: Not auto-synced after creation

what_it_does: Threaded, categorised forum per repository or organisation
research_use: Methodological debate, planning, open questions not tied to a task
traceability: Persistent, searchable, linkable record
limitations: Separate from issues; cannot be added to a Project directly

what_it_does: Q&A, Announcements, Ideas, Poll and open-ended discussion types
research_use: Structure discussion; Q&A for recurring methods questions
traceability: Category is a filterable attribute
limitations: Fixed category formats

what_it_does: Accept one reply in a Q&A discussion as the answer
research_use: Capture the resolved methodological answer
traceability: A decision-like, highlighted record
limitations: One answer per discussion; no rationale field

what_it_does: Multiple-choice poll inside a discussion
research_use: Lightweight group decision (which method, which tool)
traceability: Vote counts are recorded
limitations: No weighting; not configurably anonymous

what_it_does: Independent line of commits from a base
research_use: Alternative analyses, manuscript drafts, experimental methods in parallel
traceability: Each line of work keeps its own attributable history
limitations: Requires Git literacy; long-lived branches drift

what_it_does: Require PRs, reviews and status checks; block force-push; restrict pushers; require signed commits
research_use: Protect the main analysis and manuscript; enforce review before merge
traceability: Guarantees changes to protected refs went through a reviewed PR
plan_availability: public repos all plans; private needs Team+
limitations: Key enforcement is paid for private repos

what_it_does: Diff any two branches, tags or commits
research_use: See how analysis variants or draft versions diverge
traceability: Divergence is explicit and shareable
limitations: Large diffs are hard to review

what_it_does: Proposed merge of a branch with diff, discussion and checks
research_use: Structured review of analysis code, manuscript sections, methodology changes
traceability: Bundles rationale, diff, approvals and linked issues into one record
limitations: Review-by-diff suits text/code better than some artifact types

what_it_does: Approve / request-changes / comment states with threaded line comments
research_use: Internal peer review of research artifacts
traceability: Who approved what, and when, is recorded
limitations: Approvals can be dismissed; culture-dependent

what_it_does: Enforce N approvals or owner approval before merge
research_use: Guarantee that stats/data/manuscript changes get the right reviewer
traceability: Merge is blocked without the mandated review
limitations: Paid for private; can be bypassed by admins

what_it_does: Reviewer proposes an exact edit that the author commits with one click
research_use: Concrete manuscript or code fixes with reviewer attribution
traceability: The suggested edit and its acceptance are both in history
limitations: Small edits only

what_it_does: 'Development'-linked issues that auto-close on merge
research_use: Bind a task to the change set that completed it
traceability: Task-to-evidence link recorded on both sides
limitations: Manual linking; one direction of automation

what_it_does: Default checklist shown when a PR is opened
research_use: Enforce review gates ('results reproduced? data documented?')
traceability: Checklist state is part of the PR record
limitations: Not enforced; contributors can ignore items

what_it_does: YAML automation triggered by events, running jobs on hosted runners
research_use: Validation, tests, doc/figure regeneration, release packaging, reproducibility checks
traceability: Each run is logged with its trigger, commit and output
plan_availability: all plans (minutes quota; free for public)
limitations: Real engineering effort; YAML and CI knowledge needed

what_it_does: Run on push, PR, schedule, manual dispatch or release
research_use: Check on every change; nightly data validation; archive on release
traceability: Automation is tied to specific repository events
limitations: Some triggers have edge cases and quotas

what_it_does: Time-based workflow runs
research_use: Recurring link checks, data refresh, backups
traceability: Regular automated checkpoints
limitations: Delayed or disabled after repo inactivity

what_it_does: Upload run outputs; render a Markdown summary per run
research_use: Keep generated figures/reports per run; human-readable check results
traceability: Outputs and check results are attached to a specific run/commit
limitations: Artifact retention is capped; not archival

what_it_does: Run a job across combinations of versions, OSes or parameters
research_use: Test an analysis across R/Python versions or datasets
traceability: Cross-environment results recorded together
limitations: Consumes minutes quickly

what_it_does: Credentialed steps with protected secrets and deploy environments
research_use: Automated deposit to an external archive (e.g. Zenodo) on release
traceability: Credentialed actions are scoped and logged
limitations: Security-sensitive; misconfiguration risk

what_it_does: Share workflow definitions across repositories
research_use: Standardise research automation across a group's projects
traceability: Shared automation is itself versioned
limitations: Versioning of the shared workflow must be managed

what_it_does: Named, notes-bearing package tied to a tag, with attached assets
research_use: Citable project snapshot (v1.0 paper), dataset or software version
traceability: Fixed point linked to a commit and to the work merged since the last release
limitations: Assets are not archival; ~2 GB per file

what_it_does: Compiles notes from merged PRs and contributors since the last tag
research_use: Automatic changelog of what changed between versions
traceability: Version-to-version change summary derived from PR history
limitations: Only as good as the PR titles and labels

what_it_does: Enabling the GitHub-Zenodo webhook mints a DOI and archives each release
research_use: Persistent identifier and long-term preservation for outputs
traceability: Each released version gets an external, citable, preserved record
limitations: Third-party service; the canonical bridge for archiving

what_it_does: Graded permissions: read, triage, write, maintain, admin
research_use: PI as admin, collaborators write, reviewers triage, public read
traceability: Who can do what is explicit
limitations: Coarse below Enterprise; per-repo

what_it_does: Controls who can see the repository
research_use: Private during the work, public at publication; internal within an institution
traceability: Disclosure state is explicit and changeable
limitations: Flipping to public exposes full history

what_it_does: Independent server-side copy that can open PRs back upstream
research_use: External-contributor workflow; reuse of the project template
traceability: Contributions from outside collaborators are attributable via PRs
limitations: Fork history can diverge; syncing is manual

what_it_does: Dashboards of commits, contributors, code frequency and network
research_use: Project-activity transparency and contribution overview
traceability: Activity is summarised from the underlying history
limitations: Aggregate only; some views need a public repo

what_it_does: Per-repo and per-thread event feeds and subscriptions
research_use: Stay aware of changes to tasks, discussions and artifacts
traceability: Awareness, not a record
limitations: Notification overload; not evidence of anything

what_it_does: Record of administrative actions in an organisation
research_use: Governance record of access and configuration changes
traceability: Admin actions are logged and reviewable
limitations: Organisation-scoped; retention varies by plan

what_it_does: Tracks declared dependencies and proposes version updates
research_use: Keep a computational environment's dependencies current and recorded
traceability: Dependency changes arrive as reviewable PRs
limitations: Ecosystem coverage varies; noise if unmanaged
